title: Affine quasi-coherent complex reconstructed from ordinary sections
statement: Let Y be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], A = Gamma(Y,O), and D an integer cochain complex of O_Y-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with quasi-coherent terms. Apply ordinary sections termwise to obtain a complex of A-modules, and apply associated sheaf on Spec A [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] termwise. Push this complex forward along Y.isoSpec.inv : Spec A -> Y. The resulting complex is isomorphic to D. No boundedness, perfectness, derived-category choices, or nonemptiness are assumed.

source.place: Tag 01IB (schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves), applied termwise; Tag 06Z0 (perfect-lemma-affine-compare), associated-sheaf complex construction

proof.text: Set A = Gamma(Y,O), F = pushforward along Y.isoSpec.hom, G = pushforward along its inverse, S = moduleSpecGammaFunctor and T = tilde. Define a natural isomorphism between ordinary evaluation of Y-modules at top and F followed by S. On underlying additive groups its components are identities. The scalar compatibility is Y.isoSpec.hom.appTop composed with GammaSpecIso.inv equal to the identity, by toSpecGamma_appTop and inv_hom_id. Naturality is the identity of the actual section maps.

The functors F and G form the module-sheaf equivalence given by pushforwardComp, pushforwardCongr and pushforwardId. Hence F is left adjoint to G. Restriction along Y.isoSpec.inv is also left adjoint to G, so uniqueness of left adjoints identifies F with this restriction. Mathlib proves restriction along an open immersion preserves quasi-coherence. Apply this to every term of D to obtain quasi-coherent terms of F(D). The natural tilde/Gamma counit is invertible on these terms by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. Map it to complexes; naturality gives differential compatibility and componentwise invertibility yields tilde(S(F(D))) isomorphic to F(D). Compose with tilde of the inverse termwise section comparison.

Push the preceding complex isomorphism through G. Map the natural isomorphism F followed by G isomorphic to the identity to complexes; it is pushforwardComp followed by pushforwardCongr of Y.isoSpec.hom_inv_id followed by pushforwardId. Composing gives G(tilde(Gamma(Y,D))) isomorphic to D. The construction has no boundedness or nonemptiness assumption, so applies to zero and unbounded complexes and the empty affine scheme.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01IB and 06Z0; chain-level naturality and canonical affine-chart scalar comparison proved by B2

lean.statement:
theorem affine_sections_complex_counit (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y]
    (D : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ)
    (hDqc : ∀ n : ℤ, (D.X n).IsQuasicoherent) :
    Nonempty
      (((@Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Spec Γ(Y, ⊤)).ringCatSheaf)
        (SheafOfModules.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf) _ _ _ _
        (SheafOfModules.pushforward Y.isoSpec.inv.toRingCatSheafHom)
        ⟨fun _ _ ↦ rfl⟩ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        ((@Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ (ModuleCat.{u} (Γ(Y, ⊤) : Type u))
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (Spec Γ(Y, ⊤)).ringCatSheaf) _ _ _ _
          (tilde.functor Γ(Y, ⊤)) ⟨fun _ _ ↦ tilde.map_zero⟩
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
          (((SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u}
            Y.ringCatSheaf (op ⊤)).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj D))) ≅ D)
